Core principle: production-grade full-stack engineering, high-performance WebGL 3D graphics, persistent score analytics and automated DevOps pipeline.

1. INTRODUCTION

LastZone is a high-performance full-stack tournament management and 3D zombie survival simulation platform developed as an advanced academic showcase. It combines a cinematic cyberpunk web interface, custom WebGL/Three.js 3D inspection laboratories, an embedded Unity WebGL survival game, a Spring Boot 3.3.5 enterprise REST API backend, and an ACID-compliant PostgreSQL relational database.

The project is architected as an end-to-end evolving product rather than disconnected syllabus exercises. Semantic HTML5 structures responsive tactical views; modern CSS/GSAP powers smooth scrollytelling transitions; Three.js delivers dynamic 3D model manipulation; Spring Boot and PostgreSQL provide persistent player profiles and leaderboard stats; and Jenkins automates continuous testing and containerized delivery.

1.1 Problem Statement

Online gaming tournaments demand tightly coordinated systems: sub-millisecond leaderboard synchronization, secure player authentication, immersive asset inspection, real-time match telemetry, and seamless multi-device access. Developing this end-to-end requires integrating complex front-end graphics rendering with resilient, scalable backend transactional architectures.

1.2 Proposed Solution

LastZone delivers a cohesive esports tournament platform with real-time score ingestion, dynamic 3D armory inspection (anatomical body-part targeting and weapon attachments), encrypted JWT user authentication, and high-frequency leaderboard aggregation with strict data validation.

2. ABSTRACT, OBJECTIVES AND SCOPE

2.1 Abstract

The platform implements an immersive esports web application demonstrating player registration, 3D armor/weapon inspection via Three.js with multi-angle GSAP camera tweens, Unity WebGL combat simulation, JSON-backed leaderboard queries, Spring Boot REST persistence, and containerized CI/CD execution via Jenkins and Docker.

2.2 Objectives

  • Develop a responsive, cyberpunk-themed tactical interface using semantic HTML5, modern CSS, and Vite.
  • Engineer an interactive 3D Armory Inspection suite using Three.js, OrbitControls, and targeted GSAP camera zooms.
  • Embed an interactive Unity WebGL survival game transmitting live match score packets over HTTP REST.
  • Build a Spring Boot 3.3.5 REST API with PostgreSQL persistence, JPA entities, and BCrypt password encryption.
  • Establish an automated Jenkins CI/CD pipeline executing build, test, and container packaging on every commit.

2.3 Scope

Demonstration encompasses full client-server lifecycle, 3D graphics rendering, automated score submission, and DevOps pipeline. Commercial financial transactions and production multi-region matchmaking clusters are simulated.

4.1 Request Flow

The browser initializes the client SPA and renders static and 3D scenes locally. The embedded Unity WebGL combat engine runs in an isolated canvas, capturing player survival duration, kills, and accuracy. Upon match termination, a JSON payload is dispatched via HTTP POST to the Spring Boot backend. Spring Security validates authentication tokens, Hibernate binds parameters into SQL queries, and PostgreSQL persists score records before returning status to the client.

4.2 Folder Organization

The project enforces clean separation: src/components/ (HUD, Canvas, Modals), src/pages/ (Weapons, Leaderboard, Arena), backend/src/main/java/ (Controllers, Entities, Services), backend/src/main/resources/ (schema, application.yml), and Jenkinsfile (CI/CD pipeline script).

4.3 Data Boundaries

Transient camera coordinates and audio states use sessionStorage; authenticated session JWT tokens use localStorage; persistent match scores, player stats, and historical rankings reside strictly within PostgreSQL.

13. DATABASE DESIGN

TABLE PRIMARY PURPOSE IMPORTANT CONSTRAINTS
usersPlayer credentials and profile dataUnique username and email, BCrypt hash, created_at timestamp.
scoresMatch telemetry and tournament pointsFK to users(id), positive score, positive kills count, indexed on score DESC.
tournamentsActive competition bracketsUnique tournament code, start/end timestamps, status enum (ACTIVE/CLOSED).
audit_logsSecurity and authentication audit trailFK to users(id), client IP address, action string, event timestamp.
12
Configuration: database credentials and JWT secret keys are loaded from system environment variables (POSTGRES_DB, POSTGRES_USER, JWT_SECRET). Sensitive secrets are strictly excluded from source control.

13.1 Relationship Model

One user can submit multiple score records across different tournament stages. Foreign keys implement cascading relationships to preserve referential integrity across player deletions. UTF-8 character encoding is enforced across all tables to support global player handles.

13.2 Data Integrity

Database-level constraints guarantee that negative scores or invalid survival timestamps are rejected at the storage layer. B-Tree indexes on scores(score DESC) guarantee sub-millisecond leaderboard retrieval during peak concurrency.

13.3 Fictional Seed Data

The automated schema migration script populates realistic mock tournament participants, verified scores ranging from 12,000 to 95,000 points, and sample match timestamps for testing.

14. WEBSITE ANALYZER / ASSET & PERFORMANCE ANALYZER

The asset pipeline verifies 3D GLTF asset headers, textures, and HTTP API response timings while enforcing strict payload thresholds.

Figure 14.1 — Secure player sign-in and token authentication portal

The validation suite verifies TLS termination, enforces response size limits, and profiles Three.js vertex counts to ensure 60 FPS performance on standard classroom computers.

Security boundary: the WebGL engine isolates GPU shaders within an unprivileged sandbox. Raw file system access and insecure cross-origin asset requests are blocked.
13

15. RESPONSIVE DESIGN, ACCESSIBILITY AND SECURITY

15.1 Responsive Design

CSS Grid and Flexbox establish fluid layouts across 4K desktop, laptop, tablet, and mobile viewports. Media query breakpoints dynamically re-stack HUD cards and hide intensive 3D post-processing on constrained mobile devices.

15.2 Accessibility

Semantic landmark tags (<header>, <nav>, <main>, <footer>), high-contrast ARIA roles, visible focus outlines, and keyboard shortcuts ensure comprehensive navigability.

15.3 Security Controls

  • Hibernate and Spring Data JPA parameterize all database queries, preventing SQL injection.
  • Passwords are salted and hashed using BCrypt with work factor 12 before persistence.
  • Stateless JWT tokens secure API endpoints with time-bounded expiration.
  • CORS policies restrict backend communication strictly to authorized frontend origins.
  • XSS protection is enforced by escaping all rendered player usernames in the leaderboard DOM.

23.1 Troubleshooting Guide

SYMPTOM ACTION
3D Model renders black or blank canvasVerify ambient/directional lighting in Three.js and check WebGL hardware acceleration.
Backend API returns Connection RefusedEnsure PostgreSQL service is running on port 5432 and Spring Boot is active on 8080.
Leaderboard AJAX displays network errorConfirm CORS configuration in SecurityConfig.java allows http://localhost:5173.
Jenkins build failure on Maven stageCheck Java 21 environment variables and verify pom.xml dependency versions.
